name: Kennedy Space Center Launch
company: NASA / Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex
unique: Watch a rocket leave the pad across the Indian River, then stand under an actual Saturn V, the only place you can do both in one day.
buzz: Launch days are transcendent and traffic is apocalyptic; the visitor complex alone is a full day. Buy launch-viewing tickets the day they drop.

name: Swim with Manatees
unique: In winter, hundreds of West Indian manatees crowd the warm springs, and you can snorkel beside them in clear water while they sleep, eat lettuce and ignore you.
buzz: Operators are strictly regulated and good ones brief you on no-touch rules; visibility depends on the tide. Book the earliest boat.

name: Dry Tortugas and Fort Jefferson
unique: A hexagonal brick fort on a tiny island 70 miles from Key West, surrounded by clear water and coral, reachable only by boat or seaplane.
buzz: People call it the best day trip in Florida; the ferry is long and expensive and the snorkeling is the reward. Book weeks ahead.

name: Ichetucknee Springs State Park
dates: Year round; tubing late May to early September
unique: A spring run so clear that the bottom is visible at eight feet, where visitors float downstream on tubes through cypress and eelgrass for two hours in water that stays at seventy two degrees, with a daily cap on how many people can go in.
buzz: Tubing the Ichetucknee is a Florida rite and the park limits admission because of it. Early morning is calm and clear, the afternoon is a crowd, and snorkeling in the winter is the locals' version.

name: National Naval Aviation Museum
unique: One of the largest naval aviation museums in the world, with Blue Angels jets, a World War II carrier deck and a flight simulator, free on a naval base.
buzz: Free and enormous, with planes you can walk around and climb into. Bring ID for base access.

name: Blue Spring Manatees
unique: A first-magnitude spring that becomes a winter refuge for hundreds of manatees, viewable from a boardwalk in water so clear you can count the scars on their backs.
buzz: On a cold January morning there can be 300 manatees; arrive at opening because the park fills by 9am. Swimming is closed in manatee season.

name: Edward Ball Wakulla Springs State Park
dates: Year round, boats on a schedule
unique: One of the largest and deepest freshwater springs in the world, with glass bottom boat tours over a riverbed of mastodon bones, manatees in winter, alligators, and a 1930s lodge with hand painted ceilings where Creature from the Black Lagoon was filmed.
buzz: The boat tour is the thing to book and the rangers call out manatees and turtles. The lodge and the swimming area are from another era and the water is cold and clear enough to see the bottom.

name: Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge
unique: A full-scale Star Wars outpost where the cast never breaks character, you can build a lightsaber in a secret workshop and fly the Millennium Falcon with five strangers.
buzz: Rise of the Resistance is the best ride in America by acclimation; the lines and the upcharges are the cost. Rope-drop or buy the lightning lane.

name: T.H. Stone Memorial St. Joseph Peninsula State Park
unique: Nine miles of undeveloped barrier peninsula with dunes twenty feet high, a bay side calm enough for small children and a gulf side with clear green water, plus a campground behind the dunes that books eleven months out.
buzz: People who know it call it the best beach in Florida and it stays quiet because there is nothing to buy there. The campground reservation is the hardest part and the bay side is where families with small children go.

name: Wynwood Walls
unique: A warehouse district turned open air mural museum, with monumental pieces by Shepard Fairey, OSGEMEOS and friends, surrounded by galleries, breweries and a decade of gentrification.
buzz: Worth the ticket for the curated courtyard; the surrounding streets are free and just as good. Go before noon for photos and fewer crowds.

name: Salvador Dali Museum
unique: The most comprehensive Dali collection outside Spain, in a hurricane-proof glass bubble on the waterfront, with massive canvases that reward standing close.
buzz: The building and the collection are both stunning; the free audio guide is genuinely good. Go Thursday evening for the smaller crowd.

name: Apalachicola Historic District
unique: A working waterfront town of Greek Revival cotton warehouses, sponge docks and oyster houses on the Apalachicola River, where the commercial fishing fleet still unloads and the streets behind it are a national historic district.
buzz: The oysters are the reason people come and the town is the reason they stay. It has kept its scale, and the raw bars on Water Street serve what the boats brought in that morning.

name: Bahia Honda State Park
unique: A state park on a keys island with a sand beach, a historic bridge ruin, snorkeling and campsites on the water.
buzz: The beach is one of the best in the keys and the old bridge is the photo. Book camping months ahead.

name: Bok Tower Gardens
unique: A 250 acre garden on a hill with a 205 foot Singing Tower, a carillon that plays daily and a pine forest that feels like Georgia.
buzz: The tower and the carillon concert are the reason, and the gardens are cool and quiet. Go for the afternoon recital.

name: Corkscrew Swamp Sanctuary
unique: A 2.25 mile boardwalk through an old growth cypress swamp, with alligators, otters and the largest nesting colony of wood storks in the country.
buzz: The boardwalk is flat and the swamp is genuinely wild. Go in winter for the birds and bring water.

name: Devil's Den Prehistoric Spring
unique: A karst window into a 54-foot deep spring under a collapsed roof, with fossil beds in the walls, sunbeams through a hole in the ceiling and 72-degree water.
buzz: Snorkelers love the cathedral light; it is small and gets crowded, so book a morning slot. Not for claustrophobic swimmers.

name: Dr. Julian G. Bruce St. George Island State Park
unique: Nine miles of undeveloped gulf beach at the end of a barrier island, with dunes, sea oats, a campground in the scrub and a bay side marsh where migratory birds drop in by the thousand in spring.
buzz: Campers book the sites a year ahead and birders come in April for the migration. The beach is wide and empty compared to the developed end of the island.

name: Fort De Soto Park
unique: A county park on five keys with a fort, a beach that regularly ranks among the best in the country, a dog beach and a ferry to Egmont Key.
buzz: The north beach is the calm one and the fort is a bonus. Parking is cheap and the sand is white.

name: J.N. Ding Darling National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A mangrove refuge on Sanibel with a wildlife drive, wading birds, alligators and a visitor center, one of the best birding spots in Florida.
buzz: The drive at low tide is the best time, and the roseate spoonbills are the prize. Bring bug spray.

name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
unique: The first undersea park in the country, with coral reefs, a sunken statue garden and snorkel and dive boats leaving from the marina.
buzz: The snorkel trip is the reason to come, and the reef is shallow enough for beginners. Book ahead in season.

name: Kissimmee Prairie Preserve State Park
dates: Year round, daylight; dry season best
unique: Fifty four thousand acres of dry prairie with cabbage palms, the largest remaining example of an imperiled habitat, where the Florida grasshopper sparrow and crested caracara live and the night sky is a certified dark sky park.
buzz: The stargazing is the reason people drive out and the birding is the reason they come back. It is flat, hot and enormous, and there is no shade, which keeps the crowds away.

name: Lady Luck Wreck Dive
dates: Year-round on scheduled dive boats; advanced certification and sea conditions required
company: South Florida Diving Headquarters and Shipwreck Park Pompano Beach
customer: Advanced scuba divers, wreck photographers, artificial-reef students
unique: The 324-foot former New York sludge tanker Newtown Creek became the Lady Luck artificial reef in 2016, with Dennis McDonald's casino-themed octopus dealers, card sharks and slot machines installed on deck.
buzz: The underwater casino gives the wreck a specific visual identity beyond a rusting hull. Depths run roughly 60–130 feet, so this is an advanced boat dive, not a snorkel stop, and the standard charter price does not include a full gear package.

name: Morikami Museum and Japanese Gardens
unique: A Japanese garden and museum built around a 1900s farming colony, with a tea house, koi ponds, bonsai and a taiko drum festival.
buzz: The gardens are genuinely serene and the museum explains the Japanese settlement of Florida. The bonsai collection is excellent.

name: Pensacola Beach
unique: A barrier island beach of sugar white sand and emerald water, with a pier, a boardwalk and the Blue Angels practicing overhead.
buzz: The sand is the best on the Gulf and the water is clear. Parking costs in the main lots.

name: Ringling Museum
unique: A circus magnate's Venetian Gothic mansion, a 21-gallery art museum and a circus museum with the actual train car and wardrobe of the greatest show on earth.
buzz: The circus museum is the surprise hit with kids; the house tour and grounds are gorgeous at sunset. Ticket bundles are worth it.

name: Siesta Key Beach
unique: A wide beach of quartz white sand that stays cool underfoot, with a lagoon, volleyball courts and a drum circle on Sundays.
buzz: The sand is the story and the sunset drum circle is the local ritual. Parking fills early.

name: St. Marks National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Seventy thousand acres of coastal marsh, pine flatwoods and impoundments along the Big Bend, with a seven mile drive to an 1842 lighthouse, wintering ducks by the thousand and the best migration birding in north Florida.
buzz: The lighthouse at the end of the drive is the photograph everybody takes and the impoundments in winter are full of birds. Alligators sun on the levee roads and photographers come for the fall migration.

name: Torreya State Park
unique: Bluffs above the Apalachicola River that rise more than a hundred and fifty feet, the steepest hiking in Florida, with the rare torreya tree, a 1930s CCC built stone lodge and a view of river swamp that looks like mountains from the top.
buzz: Hikers say it is the only place in Florida that feels like a mountain state and the climb out of the ravine is real. Botanists come for the endemic trees and the fall color is the best in the panhandle.

name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
unique: A 1916 Italian Renaissance villa on Biscayne Bay, built by an industrialist with European rooms, formal gardens and a stone barge breakwater.
buzz: The house and the gardens are equally good, and the bay terrace is the photo. Go early before the tour buses.

name: Butterfly World
dates: Year-round; Monday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m., Sunday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; last entry 4 p.m.
customer: Families, gardeners, photographers, butterfly and bird visitors
unique: Screened tropical gardens at Tradewinds Park support thousands of flying butterflies and birds, with a lorikeet encounter and planted pathways that put visitors inside the enclosure rather than behind glass.
buzz: Arriving by midafternoon leaves enough time before the butterfly area closes at 4:30 p.m. Lorikeet nectar is a small separate cash purchase, and weather can alter operations, so this is not a rushed final stop of the day.

name: SS Copenhagen and Shipwreck Snorkel Trail
cost: Free self-guided; boat charter and rental gear extra
dates: Year-round in calm sea conditions; SS Copenhagen requires a boat
company: Town of Lauderdale-by-the-Sea and local dive charters
unique: The 1900 British steamer wreck rests in roughly 15–30 feet of water as a state underwater archaeological preserve, while a separate Datura Avenue snorkel trail and nearshore reefs offer a beach-accessible alternative.
buzz: Do not confuse the two sites. The Copenhagen is about three-quarters of a mile offshore and needs a boat and mooring buoy; the Datura trail is in about 10 feet of water. Visibility and surge determine whether either is worthwhile.

name: Ski Rixen USA Cable Wakeboarding
dates: Year-round, Tuesday–Friday 2–7 p.m., weekends noon–7 p.m.; closed Monday; registered weekend lessons 10 a.m.–noon
company: Ski Rixen USA at Quiet Waters Park
customer: Wakeboard beginners, water-sports travelers, teenagers, active groups
unique: A full-size overhead cable more than 2,700 feet long pulls riders around a Quiet Waters lake without a boat, with beginner lessons, continuous laps and optional ramps and rails for experienced riders.
buzz: The basic two-hour pass includes ride time and some equipment, but wakeboard and obstacle-ready rentals cost more. Beginners should book the slower weekend lesson block instead of arriving during open riding and expecting instruction.

name: Skydive Zephyrhills
customer: First timers, young adults, bucket listers
unique: One of the largest drop zones in the world, with a 14,000-foot tandem jump over flat Florida farmland and the Gulf beyond, no mountains, just the horizon.
buzz: Tandem instructors get consistent praise for calming nerves; video packages are worth it. Weather delays are common in summer.

name: Anna Maria Island
unique: A seven mile barrier island of white sand, a wooden pier, a village of cottages and a free trolley that runs the length of it.
buzz: The trolley makes it easy without a car, and the beach is wide and calm. Sunsets at the pier are the ritual.

name: Anne Kolb Nature Center and West Lake Park
cost: Free nature center; rentals and some park entrances extra
dates: Year-round; nature center daily 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; park 8 a.m.–6 p.m.; marina usually Saturday–Monday, weather permitting
unique: A 1,500-acre coastal mangrove estuary with marked paddling trails, a 68-foot observation tower, a 3,500-gallon aquarium and an exhibit hall explaining the ecology of West Lake.
buzz: The tower and aquarium make an easy short visit, but the mangrove trails are the fuller experience. The rental marina keeps a shorter, weather-dependent schedule than the nature center, so call before planning around a paddle.

name: Apalachicola Bluffs and Ravines Preserve
dates: October to April, guided and reserved access
unique: The Garden of Eden Trail drops off the bluff into steephead ravines where cool seeps keep plants that survive nowhere else, down to the Apalachicola River and back up, on land managed to restore the longleaf and ravine forest.
buzz: The climb back out is the hardest mile in the panhandle and the ravines are genuinely strange for Florida. Access is by reservation and the quiet is part of the deal.

name: Blackwater River State Park
unique: A sand bottomed river running clear and amber through longleaf pine flatwoods, with white sand bars for stopping, a swimming area and a campground, on a designated state paddling trail that runs for miles.
buzz: Paddlers call it the best family river in the panhandle because the current is gentle and the sand is white. On summer weekends the put in fills by nine.

name: Castillo de San Marcos
unique: The oldest masonry fort in the continental United States, built from coquina shell stone that absorbed cannonballs, on the oldest continuously occupied European street grid in the country.
buzz: Rangers fire cannons on weekends; the walls are fun to climb and the history is brutal and well told. Combine with the old town at dusk.

name: Circle B Bar Reserve
unique: A 1,200 acre former ranch turned wetland preserve with a boardwalk, oak hammocks and alligators everywhere, one of the best wildlife walks in central Florida.
buzz: The alligators are close and the birds are abundant. Go early and stay on the path.

name: Daytona International Speedway
unique: The 2.5 mile superspeedway where NASCAR's biggest race runs, with a track tour, a museum and the banked turns you can walk on.
buzz: The track tour is the way to feel the banks, and the 500 is the bucket list event. Book tours ahead.

name: Dr. Von D. Mizell-Eula Johnson State Park
dates: Year-round, daily 8 a.m. to sunset; construction and facility notices apply
customer: Beach visitors, civil-rights history readers, anglers, birders
unique: A 310-acre barrier beach beside Port Everglades preserves 2.5 miles of undeveloped coast and tells the history of the segregated beach and the wade-in campaigns led by Eula Johnson, Dr. Von D. Mizell and others.
buzz: The beach and the civil-rights history reward equal time. Port dredging and north-jetty work began in 2025 and 2026, with some work expected through early 2028, so check current access and restroom closures before a long visit.

name: Everglades Airboat
unique: A flat-bottomed fan boat skims a sawgrass river at 40mph, stopping for alligators, herons and the strange silence of the actual swamp.
buzz: Coopertown is the oldest operator and gets praise for real guides; the souvenir-photo upsell is universal. Bring ear protection for kids.

name: Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden
unique: Eighty three acres of tropical plants, with a rainforest, a butterfly conservatory, a palm collection and a tram tour.
buzz: The butterfly house and the tram are the easy wins, and the collection is world class. Hot in summer, so go early.

name: Fisheating Creek
dates: Year round, best November to May
unique: A blackwater creek running into Lake Okeechobee through cypress swamp so thick that the water and the trees are the only things visible for miles, with a campground and canoe rentals on the bank.
buzz: Paddlers call it the closest thing to a jungle in Florida and the alligators are everywhere and uninterested. The campground is basic and the nights are loud with frogs.

name: Florida Caverns State Park
dates: Year round, tours daily on the hour
unique: The only Florida state park with dry cave tours open to the public, where a ranger walks you through limestone chambers of stalactites, flowstone and soda straws carved by water draining through the Marianna lowlands.
buzz: The tour is the reason to come and the guides make the geology land. The cave stays cool in summer, the tour sells out on holidays and the campground and trails are the quiet part.

name: Florida Museum of Natural History
unique: A free museum with a butterfly rainforest, fossil skeletons, Florida's native cultures and a giant shark jaw, on the UF campus.
buzz: The butterfly rainforest is the kid hit and the fossils are serious. Free, with a small fee for the butterfly house.

name: Fort Clinch State Park
customer: Families, history travellers, beach walkers, cyclists
unique: A brick and tabby Third System fort begun in 1847 on the north end of Amelia Island, never finished and never fired on in anger, with restored barracks, a garrison of uniformed interpreters on the first weekend of the month and a beach below the walls.
buzz: The fort is the reason to come and the beach and the shaded campground are the reason to stay. The candlelight tour and the living history weekends are the ones locals plan around.

name: Grayton Beach State Park
unique: A state park with dunes, a coastal dune lake, a beach of white sand and campsites under scrub oak, on Scenic 30A.
buzz: The beach is quieter than the towns and the dune lake is unusual. Book camping early.

name: Gulfstream Park Championship Meet
dates: Seasonal race meets; Championship Meet live racing Thursday–Sunday; Pegasus World Cup January 30, 2027
customer: Horse-racing visitors, sports groups, handicappers, event travelers
unique: Thoroughbred racing at the 1939 Hallandale track centers on the paddock, walking ring and stretch run, with the Championship Meet, Florida Derby and January Pegasus World Cup forming distinct levels of race-day visit.
buzz: An ordinary race afternoon is a different purchase from Pegasus or a packaged tasting event. Watch the horses in the walking ring before a race and check reserved-seat pricing, since marquee dates and hospitality packages cost much more.

name: Highlands Hammock State Park
unique: One of Florida's oldest state parks, protecting an old growth hammock of live oak, cabbage palm and cypress with a boardwalk, a tram tour, a CCC era camp and trails where panthers and black bears have been recorded.
buzz: The giant oaks and the boardwalk through the swamp are the reasons people come, and the tram is the easy version. It is the oldest park in the system and locals treat it as a family inheritance.

name: Jonathan Dickinson State Park
unique: Eleven thousand acres of sand pine scrub, river swamp and mangrove along the Loxahatchee River, with a canoe trail through a federally designated wild and scenic river, a campground and a hill that is actually a hill.
buzz: The Loxahatchee paddle is the reason to come and the cypress swamp upstream is the best part of it. Cyclists use the paved roads and the campground is one of the biggest in the state.

name: Juniper Springs Recreation Area
company: U.S. Forest Service, Ocala National Forest
unique: A spring built into a CCC era stone and concrete swimming basin with a mill house and a run that paddlers follow downstream through the Ocala National Forest to Juniper Creek.
buzz: The stone basin is beautiful and the water is cold, and the paddle down Juniper Creek is a half day of narrow twisting water. It is the busiest spring in the forest and still worth it on a weekday.

name: Kingsley Plantation
unique: A sea island cotton plantation with the planter's house and the tabby slave cabins still standing, on a marsh island in the Timucuan preserve.
buzz: The slave cabins are the powerful part, and the ranger talks are excellent. Free.

name: Little Havana
unique: A Cuban neighborhood centered on Calle Ocho, with cigar rollers, ventanitas, domino players at Maximo Gomez Park and croquetas on every block.
buzz: Go hungry and walk Calle Ocho, then sit in the domino park. The cigar shops are happy to show you how it is done.

name: Loggerhead Marinelife Center
unique: A sea turtle hospital with tanks of recovering turtles, a surgical suite and nesting beach programs, free to visit.
buzz: The turtles are close and the staff explain the injuries and the nesting season. Free, with a donation suggested.

name: Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A 140,000 acre refuge beside the space center, with a wildlife drive, manatees, alligators and some of the best birding in the state.
buzz: The Black Point drive is the easy win, especially in winter for waterfowl. Bring binoculars and bug spray.

name: Myakka River State Park
unique: One of the oldest and largest state parks, with a canopy walkway, a river boat tour, alligators and a grassy prairie.
buzz: The canopy walk and the boat tour are the two things to do, and the gators are everywhere. Go early.

name: NSU Art Museum Fort Lauderdale
dates: Year-round; Tuesday–Saturday 11 a.m.–5 p.m., Sunday noon–5 p.m.; closed Monday
customer: Art museum visitors, modern-art readers, couples, architecture people
unique: A permanent collection of more than 7,500 works includes substantial CoBrA holdings and the largest collection of William J. Glackens's work and archives, alongside African, Oceanic and Americas art.
buzz: The Glackens and CoBrA holdings distinguish this from a general contemporary-art stop. Sunday public tours run at 2 p.m., and the first Thursday of each month is free with hours extended to 7 p.m.

name: Paynes Prairie Preserve State Park
unique: A 21,000 acre prairie with wild horses, bison, alligators and a boardwalk, plus a sinkhole that once drained a lake.
buzz: The bison and horses are a surprise in Florida, and the observation tower is the view. Bring bug spray.

name: Sebring International Raceway
customer: Sports car fans, racing travellers, families
unique: America's oldest road racing circuit, laid out on a World War Two bomber training base, where the 12 Hours of Sebring has run since 1950 and the concrete and the bumps are the same ones the greats drove on.
buzz: Endurance racing people treat it as a pilgrimage and the March race is a camping festival with cars. The track is rough and the history is the appeal.

name: Silver Springs State Park
unique: A first magnitude spring with glass bottom boat tours, kayak rentals and monkeys in the trees, one of Florida's oldest attractions.
buzz: The glass bottom boat is the classic and the spring water is impossibly clear. Kayaking is the better way to see it.

name: Spirit of the Suwannee Music Park
dates: Year round; big festivals in spring and fall
company: Spirit of the Suwannee Music Park
unique: Eight hundred acres on the Suwannee with a covered amphitheater, a restaurant and enough camping to hold a festival, hosting multi day bluegrass, jam and roots events that draw people from across the country.
buzz: Festival regulars describe it as a Florida institution with a river to swim in when the music stops. The campground fills and people come back every year with the same group.

name: St. Andrews State Park
unique: A park on the pass between the Gulf and St. Andrews Bay, with a snorkeling jetty, a shell island ferry and a beach that stays calm.
buzz: The jetty snorkeling is the draw, with fish and clear water. Good for kids.

name: Steinhatchee Scalloping
company: Local marinas and guides at Steinhatchee
unique: A shallow grass flat off the Big Bend where you snorkel for bay scallops in three to six feet of water, then take them back to a dock where somebody will clean and cook them for you.
buzz: Families plan summer vacations around it and the season is short. The river town has no beach, which keeps the crowds down, and everybody comes back with a cooler.

name: Suwannee River Wilderness Trail
cost: Free, cabin and shuttle fees extra
dates: Year round, best October to May
unique: A mapped paddling route with river camps and cabins spaced along the Suwannee from White Springs to the Gulf, so a paddler can go for a day or a week and sleep on the bank every night.
buzz: Paddlers plan the whole river in sections and the river camps have made it possible. The water is dark, the banks are limestone, and the current runs the right direction.

name: Wekiwa Springs State Park
unique: An emerald spring feeding the Wekiwa River minutes from Orlando, with a swimming basin, a paddling trail through tropical hammock, and trails into sandhill where black bears and gopher tortoises live.
buzz: The spring is the swimming hole for half of north Orlando and the parking lot fills by ten on summer weekends. Paddlers go downstream and the crowds disappear within a mile.

name: Brian Piccolo Park Velodrome
cost: $25 annual individual track pass; program and event fees vary
dates: Year-round scheduled training, certification and races; check organizer calendar before visiting
company: Broward County Parks and Florida Velodrome Association
customer: Cyclists, track-racing spectators, skaters, youth athletes
unique: A 333.3-meter concrete track with banking up to about 30 degrees, a 200-meter infield warm-up track and lights supports certification, youth training, racing and inline skating in one county facility.
buzz: This is not a turn-up-on-a-road-bike attraction. Rider certification and organizer schedules matter, while spectators can target a published race. A 2026 youth program used Tuesday evenings and county documents still list annual track passes.

name: Cap's Place Island Restaurant
dates: Year-round dinner, Wednesday–Sunday from 5:30 p.m.; closed Monday and Tuesday
customer: Food-history travelers, seafood diners, couples, boaters
unique: A restaurant built on an old barge and reached by Cap's motor launch preserves its origins as the 1928 Club Unique, a Prohibition-era speakeasy, gambling spot and seafood house on a Lighthouse Point peninsula.
buzz: The launch, rough timber building and rum-running history are as much of the meal as the catch and hearts-of-palm salad. This is a dinner reservation, not a casual lunchtime stop, and hours can vary.

name: Dania Beach Invitational Jai Alai
dates: Seasonal tournament; January 5–March 31, 2027, with matinees and evening sessions; verify each year's schedule
customer: Sports curious travelers, history visitors, bettors, nightlife groups
unique: Professional pelotaris use curved cestas to hurl the pelota off the three-walled court at the 1953 Dania fronton, keeping a South Florida gambling and sporting institution visible to spectators.
buzz: The speed of the ball and the rhythm of the scoring are easier to follow in the small fronton than on a stream. This is now a limited invitational season, not the old year-round schedule, and the operator notes that seats are limited.

name: Everglades Hovercraft
unique: A hovercraft glides over sawgrass, mud and shallow water where no boat can go, into mangrove tunnels and abandoned clam camps at the edge of the Ten Thousand Islands.
buzz: The ride is smoother and louder than an airboat; reviews say the small-group trips beat the big-tour buses. Bring sunscreen and earplugs.

name: Museum of Discovery and Science
dates: Year-round; Monday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., Sunday noon–5 p.m.
customer: Families, science visitors, curious adults, rainy-day travelers
unique: Two floors combine Florida ecosystems and live animal ambassadors with aviation, engineering, a makerspace, live science demonstrations and the large-format AutoNation IMAX theater.
buzz: The scheduled animal encounters, KaBoom demonstrations and makerspace activities reward checking the daily calendar rather than wandering without a plan. Combination tickets can include HoloTheater and an IMAX documentary.

name: Solomon's Castle
unique: A castle built from scrap aluminum and salvaged stained glass by an artist who lived in it, filled with wooden machines, painted ceilings and a 60 foot replica of a Spanish galleon.
buzz: It is gloriously eccentric and the tour is funny; the boat tour and the restaurant are extras. Worth the drive inland.

name: Anastasia State Park
unique: A state park on a barrier island with a wide beach, dunes, a salt marsh and campsites under oaks, minutes from the old city.
buzz: The beach is quieter than the city beaches and the camping is shaded. Good for a combination history and beach day.

name: Bergeron Rodeo Grounds
dates: Event-driven year-round; Wednesday barrel racing and rodeos on the Town of Davie calendar
unique: Davie's longtime rodeo arena still anchors its western-themed downtown with professional and youth rodeos, barrel racing and the Orange Blossom Rodeo rather than presenting cowboy culture only as storefront decoration.
buzz: Choose an actual rodeo or barrel-racing date, since the grounds are otherwise an event venue. The 2026 calendar included Wednesday barrel racing, professional rodeos and the November Southeast Circuit Finals.

name: Blowing Rocks Preserve
unique: A limestone shoreline where waves blast water through rock holes at high tide, the largest Anastasia limestone outcrop on the Atlantic coast.
buzz: Go at high tide with a northeast wind for the blowholes, and wear shoes on the rock.

name: Chassahowitzka River
unique: A spring fed river with clear water, cypress and mangrove tunnels, manatees in winter and a campground at the launch.
buzz: The paddle is easy and the spring runs are beautiful. Rent a kayak at the campground and go early.

name: Cummer Museum of Art and Gardens
unique: A riverfront museum with European and American painting, porcelain and formal gardens on the St. Johns, with free admission on some days.
buzz: The gardens on the river are as good as the collection, and the free days make it a bargain.

name: Edison and Ford Winter Estates
unique: The winter estates of Thomas Edison and Henry Ford, with their houses, laboratories, a 1929 botanical garden and Edison's rubber research.
buzz: The labs are the interesting part and the banyan tree is enormous. Allow two hours.

name: Ernest Hemingway Home and Museum
unique: The Spanish colonial house where Hemingway wrote in the 1930s, with his furniture, his typewriter and dozens of polydactyl cats descended from his own.
buzz: The cats are the fun and the writing studio is the history. Tours run continuously and are worth the ticket.

name: Fernandina Beach Historic District
unique: A Victorian shrimping town on Amelia Island with a main street of clapboard storefronts and live oaks, a harbor full of shrimp boats, and a history that runs from Spanish and British occupation to a pirate raid and the modern shrimp fleet.
buzz: The shrimp boats are the photograph and the restaurants serve what they catch. It is walkable in an afternoon and busy on spring weekends.

name: Flagler Museum
cost: $28 adult, $14 ages 6 to 12, free age 5 and under
dates: Tuesday through Saturday 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., Sunday noon to 5 p.m., closed Monday
customer: Gilded Age history readers, architecture people, rail fans, first-time Palm Beach visitors
unique: Henry Flagler's 1902 Whitehall estate is a National Historic Landmark where visitors can walk through the Gilded Age rooms and take a first-floor docent tour included with admission.
buzz: The included docent tours add the family and railroad story that a self-guided room-by-room walk can miss. Tours run at set times, so check the schedule before arriving.

name: History Fort Lauderdale Museum Campus
dates: Year-round, daily 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; docent tours at 1, 2 and 3 p.m.
customer: Local-history readers, researchers, architecture visitors, families
unique: The 1905 New River Inn, 1907 Pioneer House and 1899 Ivy Cromartie Schoolhouse form a museum campus on the river, with artist studios and a research library holding photographs, maps and architectural drawings.
buzz: The guided three-museum ticket gives more context than a quick self-guided room circuit. The campus is compact, but the archival photo collection and artists-in-residence make it more than a period-house tour.

name: Hollywood Hot Glass Class
dates: Year-round, Wednesday–Sunday 1–9 p.m.; class booking required
customer: Maker travelers, couples, families, art students
unique: Inside ArtsPark at Young Circle, beginners work with an instructor and molten glass to shape and color a piece of their own rather than merely watching a demonstration.
buzz: The hands-on portion is about 20 minutes, so the appeal is concentrated rather than a full afternoon. Glass needs roughly 12 hours to cool, which means planning a later pickup during Wednesday-to-Sunday gallery hours.

name: Hugh Taylor Birch State Park
dates: Year-round, daily 8 a.m. to sunset; ranger walks Friday and Saturday
customer: Walkers, birders, paddlers, cyclists, beach visitors
unique: Hugh Taylor Birch's former 180-acre Terramar estate preserves maritime hammock, coastal dune lakes and a 1.9-mile park drive between the Intracoastal Waterway and the ocean.
buzz: The contrast with the surrounding beach development is the draw. Friday and Saturday ranger walks are included with admission. The floating dock has been closed since May 11, 2026, so check current paddling access.

name: Mallory Square Sunset
unique: A nightly street festival that exists only to watch the sun go down: buskers, sword swallowers, cats on tightropes and a crowd that applauds the horizon.
buzz: It is touristy and completely charming; locals avoid it and visitors remember it. Get there an hour before sunset for a seat on the pier.

name: Mike Roess Gold Head Branch State Park
unique: A ravine cut into the sandy ridge by a spring fed branch, with CCC built stone cabins and a mill from the 1930s, a swimming area, trails down into the ravine and camping in the sandhills above.
buzz: The ravine is the surprise in flat country and the CCC stone work is beautiful. Campers say it is the quietest park near Jacksonville and the swimming is cold and clear.

name: Mission San Luis
unique: A reconstructed 17th century Spanish mission and Apalachee village, with a council house, a friary and living history demonstrations.
buzz: The reconstruction is convincing and the staff explain the collision of Spanish and Apalachee life. Good for kids.

name: National Navy UDT-SEAL Museum
unique: A museum on the beach where the frogmen trained, with boats, dive gear, a bin Laden raid exhibit and the history of naval special warfare.
buzz: The artifacts are real and the stories are intense. Good for teenagers and adults.

name: Naval Air Station Fort Lauderdale Museum
dates: Year-round, Saturday and Sunday 11 a.m.–3 p.m.; last tour 2:30 p.m.; closed major holidays
company: Naval Air Station Fort Lauderdale Museum
customer: Aviation readers, veterans, World War II visitors, families
unique: A volunteer-run museum at the wartime torpedo-bomber training base preserves letters, photographs and artifacts from Flight 19, the five Avengers that disappeared after leaving Fort Lauderdale on December 5, 1945.
buzz: The documents and volunteer knowledge are the reasons to visit, not a large aircraft collection. Hours are limited to weekends, and the Flight 19 material separates the training flight and failed search from later Bermuda Triangle mythology.

name: Pelican Island National Wildlife Refuge
unique: The first national wildlife refuge in the country, set aside by Theodore Roosevelt to protect pelicans, with a boardwalk and a bird's eye view of the lagoon.
buzz: The history is the story and the birding is excellent in winter. Quiet and free.

name: Ponce Inlet Lighthouse
unique: The tallest lighthouse in Florida, with 203 steps, a keeper's quarters museum and a view of the inlet and the ocean.
buzz: The climb is hot but the view is worth it, and the museum explains the lighthouse keepers.

name: Shiva Vishnu Temple of South Florida
dates: Year-round with split morning and evening hours; check festival calendar and worship etiquette
company: Shiva Vishnu Temple of South Florida
customer: Temple-architecture visitors, Hindu worshippers, art and religion students
unique: A traditional Dravidian temple designed under chief architect Ganapati Sthapati, with entrance and shrine towers, work by sculptors from Mahabalipuram and distinct Chola, Pandya, Vijayanagara and Kerala architectural references.
buzz: The carved forms and active ritual life make this a place of worship first and an architecture visit second. The temple closes between daily sessions on weekdays and weekends, so check hours and dress and photography expectations before entering.

name: Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve
unique: A 3,500 acre wetland preserve with a 1.2 mile boardwalk through cypress, ferns and orchids, with otters, herons and alligators.
buzz: The boardwalk is easy and cool, and the wildlife is close. A good break from the beach.

name: St. Pete Pier
unique: A 26 acre pier district with a modern pier head, a beach, restaurants, a playground and a tram, on Tampa Bay.
buzz: The design is the attraction and the sunset is the show. Free to walk, with paid parking.

name: Suwannee River State Park
unique: The confluence of the Withlacoochee and the Suwannee, with bluff trails above the water, a cemetery and earthworks from a Civil War crossing, a boat ramp and a campground in the longleaf pines.
buzz: The bluff trail along the confluence is the hike and the river is the swim. Paddlers use it as a base for the Suwannee and the campground is one of the better ones in north Florida.

name: Vortex Spring
unique: A spring that pumps out millions of gallons a day at a constant sixty eight degrees, with a cavern mouth that drops into a mapped cave system, a dive training platform, a swimming area and a campground on five hundred acres.
buzz: Divers train here because the water is clear and the cavern is accessible, and families swim the basin on the same day. The dive shop and the rules are taken seriously, which is the point.

name: Wacissa River
dates: Year round, best spring and fall
company: Local outfitters and the Northwest Florida Water Management District
unique: A spring fed river running clear and fast out of a swamp north of the Aucilla, with a public ramp, eelgrass and turtles visible from the boat and enough current to make the paddle downstream effortless.
buzz: Paddlers call it the clearest small river in north Florida and the alligators are numerous and calm. Outfitters run shuttles from Wacissa and the summer weekends get busy.

name: Weeki Wachee Mermaid Show
unique: Women in mermaid tails perform underwater ballet in a natural spring theater, breathing through hoses, since 1947, the last of a vanished genre of roadside attraction.
buzz: It is gloriously retro and the performers are genuinely athletic; the park's river cruise is a nice add. Kids are mesmerized.

name: Ybor City
customer: Young adults, food people, history people
unique: A historic cigar district of brick factories, mutual aid halls and rooster-filled streets, now bars, cigar shops and Cuban restaurants.
buzz: Walk 7th Avenue, watch a cigar roller and eat a Cuban sandwich. Busy and loud on weekend nights.

name: Everglades Holiday Park Airboat Tour
dates: Year-round, daily from 9 a.m.; last full 60-minute tour 4 p.m.; weather and water levels affect trips
customer: First-time Everglades visitors, families, wildlife watchers
unique: A 60-minute airboat run from the Griffin Road edge of the Everglades combines sawgrass and open-water wildlife habitat with a separate alligator presentation by the park associated with the Gator Boys television series.
buzz: The boat is the reason to go and the alligator presentation is staged entertainment. Boats depart frequently, but arriving 30 minutes early matters. The last 4:30 p.m. boat is only a 30-minute ride.

name: Markham Park Mountain Bike Trails
cost: $5–$15; daily trail pass or membership, park entry extra when charged
dates: Year-round, daily until sunset; trail fee or annual membership required
customer: Mountain bikers, adaptive riders, off-road beginners
unique: Volunteer-maintained singletrack on the Everglades edge offers roughly 14 miles of rocky and rooty riding, including a separate approximately four-mile route for off-road hand-powered recumbent bikes and less experienced riders.
buzz: The roots and limestone make this more technical than the flat map suggests. The easier handcycle-compatible route broadens access, but riders still need the required daily pass or membership and must be off the trails by sunset.

name: Round Up Line Dancing Lessons
dates: Year-round, Wednesday–Sunday; line-dance lesson 7:30 p.m. and couples lesson 8:30 p.m.
customer: Dance beginners, country-music fans, nightlife groups, couples
unique: Davie's country nightclub teaches a line dance and a couples dance before open dancing every operating night, giving a first-time visitor a structured way onto the floor rather than leaving them to watch regulars.
buzz: Arrive for the lessons instead of treating this as a late-night bar stop. Age rules and covers change by night, Sunday has an all-ages option, and the mechanical bull runs only on selected Thursdays.

name: Air Force Armament Museum
unique: A museum of bombs, missiles, guns and aircraft, with a B-52, an SR-71 and a MOAB, on the Eglin base.
buzz: The hardware is impressive and free. Bring ID for base access.

name: Alfred B. Maclay Gardens State Park
unique: A 1,200 acre estate with formal camellia and azalea gardens, a brick walk, a lake and a 1920s house.
buzz: The spring bloom is the reason, and the brick walk is beautiful. Quiet on weekdays.

name: Apalachicola National Estuarine Research Reserve
company: Florida Department of Environmental Protection and NOAA
unique: A nature center on the bay with tanks of live sturgeon, crabs and oysters, a touch tank, a diorama of the estuary and staff who explain how the river, the bay and the barrier islands make one system that produces most of the state's oysters.
buzz: It is free and the live animals are the draw for children. Adults leave understanding why the river's flow matters, which is the point of the exhibit.

name: Bonnet House Museum and Gardens
unique: A 1920s artist's estate between the beach and the intracoastal, with a shell museum, a courtyard and gardens that survived the condo boom.
buzz: The house is eccentric and personal, and the grounds are a green surprise in the middle of Fort Lauderdale. Guided tours only.

name: Cedar Key
unique: A tiny old Florida fishing and clam town on a Gulf island, with a boardwalk, a dock, clam shacks and sunsets over the marsh.
buzz: The clams and the sunset are the reasons, and the town is small enough to walk. Quiet midweek.

name: Cortez Fishing Village
company: Cortez Village and the Florida Maritime Museum
unique: One of the last working fishing villages on Florida's west coast, with net sheds, docks, a maritime museum in a 1912 schoolhouse and seafood houses that sell what the boats brought in.
buzz: The mullet and stone crab are the point and the village has kept its scale. People come for lunch and stay to walk the docks.

name: Dade Battlefield Historic State Park
dates: Year round; reenactment in early January
unique: The pine flatwoods where in December 1835 Major Francis Dade and more than a hundred soldiers were ambushed by Seminole and Black Seminole warriors, the opening fight of the Second Seminole War, with a museum, earthworks and a monument.
buzz: The January reenactment is one of the largest in the south and the park is empty the rest of the year. The museum tells the Seminole side, which is the part most accounts leave out.

name: Deering Estate
unique: A 1920s stone house on Biscayne Bay with fossil beds, a hardwood hammock and a canoe trail through the mangroves.
buzz: The house tour and the nature trail are both good, and the bay is calm for kayaking. Less crowded than Vizcaya.

name: Devil's Millhopper Geological State Park
unique: A 120 foot deep sinkhole with a boardwalk down to the bottom, fern covered walls and a miniature rainforest at the floor.
buzz: The boardwalk down is steep and cool, and the sinkhole feels like another world. Quick and cheap.

name: Fanning Springs State Park
unique: A second magnitude spring pouring sixty five million gallons a day into a swimming basin beside the Suwannee, with a boardwalk, a dive platform and live oaks over the picnic area, reachable by boat from the river.
buzz: Swimmers like that the basin is deep enough to dive and the river is right there. It is quieter than the bigger springs and the water is a constant seventy two degrees.

name: Fort Lauderdale Water Taxi
dates: Year-round, daily 10 a.m.–10 p.m.; weather and marine traffic affect service
customer: First-time visitors, boat watchers, photographers, travelers without a car
unique: A hop-on, hop-off boat circuit through the New River and Intracoastal canals links more than 30 stops in Fort Lauderdale, Pompano Beach and Hollywood, making the working waterfront and canal neighborhoods the itinerary.
buzz: Treat the full Fort Lauderdale loop as a three-hour outing rather than punctual transportation. Boats generally arrive every 30–45 minutes, and the live tracker is useful because weather, bridge openings and boat traffic cause delays.

name: Harry P. Leu Gardens
unique: Fifty acres of camellias, roses and a tropical rainforest on a lake, with a 1880s house museum and a butterfly garden.
buzz: Shady and quiet, a good break from the theme parks. The camellia collection is the winter highlight.

name: Historic Stranahan House Museum
dates: Year-round, 5–6 days weekly; daily audio tours and advance-arranged docent tours
customer: History readers, architecture visitors, first-time Fort Lauderdale visitors
unique: Frank and Ivy Stranahan's 1901 New River house preserves the trading post, ferry crossing and community rooms around which Fort Lauderdale developed, with the family's furnishings and personal history in the rooms.
buzz: The house is small and the family story carries the visit. Daily admission uses a 45-minute audio wand. Weekly availability changes with school groups and rentals, and ghost tours have been discontinued permanently.

name: Jaxson's Ice Cream Parlor and Restaurant
dates: Year-round; Sunday–Thursday 11:30 a.m.–11 p.m., Friday–Saturday until midnight; closed Thanksgiving
unique: Monroe Udell's family-run parlor has made ice cream on Federal Highway since 1956, with dozens of flavors and toppings, oversized sundaes and a dining room packed with old license plates and memorabilia.
buzz: The house-made ice cream and the cluttered room are the institution; the full savory menu is secondary for many visitors. Late hours make it useful after a flight or cruise, but expect a wait at peak dessert times.

name: Lafayette Blue Springs State Park
dates: Year round, swimming best May to September
unique: A blue spring that boils up beside the Suwannee River and spills into it over a limestone ledge, with a swimming basin, a boat ramp where the two waters meet and moss hung oaks over both.
buzz: Swimmers like that the basin is small and the river is right there, and divers come for the cave. The park is quiet and cheap and the water is cold year round.

name: Lion Country Safari
unique: A drive through safari park with lions, rhinos, giraffes and zebras loose around the car, plus a walk through amusement area.
buzz: The drive is the fun, especially for kids who have never seen a lion outside a cage. Go early when the animals are active.

name: Madison Blue Spring State Park
unique: A first magnitude spring that pours into the Withlacoochee River in a limestone bowl, with a swimming area, a dive platform and a cave system that makes it a certification site for cave divers.
buzz: Swimmers like the bowl shape and the river that runs out of it, and divers come for the cavern. The park is small and the parking fills early on summer weekends.

name: Madison Historic District
unique: A courthouse square with a ring of 1800s commercial buildings and streets of Greek Revival, Italianate and Victorian houses, in a cotton town that was one of the richest in antebellum Florida.
buzz: Architectural historians rank the district among the best small town collections in the state. The square and the four streets around it take an afternoon and there is almost nobody else walking.

name: McKee Botanical Garden
unique: Eighteen acres of tropical hammock and water lilies planted in the 1920s as a roadside attraction, with a stone bridge, a hall of ferns, a children's garden and a giant water lily pond.
buzz: The water lilies and the old stone work are the photographs and the children's garden keeps families there longer than planned. It is a 1920s roadside garden that survived and got better.

name: Naples Pier
unique: A wooden pier on a wide Gulf beach, good for fishing, dolphin watching and the sunset that draws a crowd every night.
buzz: The sunset is the event and the pier is the viewpoint. Parking is tight, so walk or bike.

name: Norton Museum of Art
cost: $20 adult, $17 senior, $5 student, free age 12 and under
dates: Open Monday and Wednesday through Saturday 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., Friday until 10 p.m., Sunday 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., closed Tuesday
customer: Art museum visitors, architecture people, date nights, curious families
unique: Palm Beach County's major art museum pairs its collection and changing exhibitions with Friday evening Art After Dark programming, giving visitors both a daytime museum visit and a nighttime way into the local art scene.
buzz: Friday evening is a different visit from a quiet weekday gallery circuit, with Art After Dark admission reduced to $10 for adults and seniors. The museum is closed Tuesday.

name: Old Dillard Museum
cost: Free; tours and programs by arrangement
dates: School-year tours and public programs; contact the museum for an appointment before visiting
customer: Black-history visitors, music fans, educators, local-history readers
unique: Fort Lauderdale's 1924 school for Black students now holds exhibits on education and community life, including a jazz room devoted to former Dillard teacher Julian Cannonball Adderley.
buzz: The building and the personal accounts are the substance, and visitors who get a guided tour report learning far more than the small galleries initially suggest. This is a school-district museum, so do not assume daily walk-in access.

name: Ravine Gardens State Park
unique: Two steephead ravines turned into a terraced azalea garden by Depression era work crews, with a two mile loop, suspension bridges, stone structures and a spring at the bottom.
buzz: In late winter when the azaleas bloom it is one of the best garden walks in the state and the rest of the year it is a shady ravine hike. The CCC and WPA stone work is still there.

name: Robert is Here
unique: A fruit stand that became a landmark, selling smoothies from fruit you have never heard of, with a petting zoo, live music and a milkshake list that runs to dozens.
buzz: The smoothies are the reason to stop on the way to the Everglades; the line moves and the exotic fruit tasting is worth it.

name: Sample-McDougald House
dates: Year-round, Tuesday–Saturday noon–4 p.m.; guided tours at noon, 1, 2 and 3 p.m.
customer: Historic-house visitors, local-history readers, architecture fans
unique: Pompano pioneer Albert Neal Sample's 1916 Georgian Revival farmhouse survives with both Sample and McDougald family furnishings after the 4,500-square-foot house was moved to Centennial Park in 2001.
buzz: The two-family story and the move explain how suburban Pompano consumed its farm landscape. The docent tour covers both floors in about 45 minutes, with foyer photographs available for visitors unable to use the stairs.

name: Seaside
unique: The planned New Urbanist town where The Truman Show was filmed, with pastel cottages, picket fences, a pavilion and a walkable center.
buzz: The architecture is the attraction and the beach is gorgeous. Busy in summer, quiet in winter.

name: St. Augustine Lighthouse
company: St. Augustine Lighthouse and Maritime Museum
unique: A black and white striped lighthouse with a maritime museum and a dark of the moon ghost tour, where staff report footsteps on the tower stairs and a girl in the basement.
buzz: The climb is worth it for the view alone; the ghost tour is one of the better researched ones in Florida. Book after dark.

name: St. Vincent Island National Wildlife Refuge
dates: Year round, daylight; access by boat
unique: A barrier island reachable only by boat with a herd of sambar deer brought from India in the 1900s, loggerhead turtles nesting in summer, and an estuary that serves as a nursery for the bay's oysters and shrimp.
buzz: Birders take the ferry for the shorebirds and the isolation. There are no facilities and no shade, and that is what keeps it empty.

name: Stephen Foster Folk Culture Center State Park
unique: A park on the Suwannee dedicated to the songwriter who never saw the river he made famous, with a carillon tower that plays daily, a museum of Florida folk life and craft demonstrations, and a campground under the oaks.
buzz: The carillon is the thing people remember and the folk life exhibits explain the Cracker culture of the river. It is quiet, cheap and the campground is a local favorite.

name: Superblue Miami
unique: A warehouse of immersive light and sound installations, including a mirrored infinity room and a cloud sculpture you walk through, designed by artists rather than set builders.
buzz: The mirrored room is the photo everyone wants and the timed entry keeps it calm; it is short for the price. Pair with the Design District.

name: Tallahassee Museum
unique: A 52 acre museum of Florida history and wildlife with a 1880s farm, a caboose, a zip line and native animals including panthers and bears.
buzz: The mix of history and animals works for kids, and the zip line is the adrenaline add on.

name: The Florida Aquarium
unique: An aquarium with a walk through wetland gallery, sharks, otters and a coral reef exhibit, plus a splash pad and a penguin encounter.
buzz: The wetland walk through is the best part and the splash pad saves a hot afternoon. Book online for a discount.

name: Washington Oaks Gardens State Park
unique: A formal garden of live oaks, camellias and azaleas on the Matanzas River side and a beach of coquina rock formations on the ocean side, in the same park, across the road from each other.
buzz: The coquina rocks at low tide are the photograph and the gardens are the quiet walk. People come for one and stay for both, and low tide is the timing that matters.

name: Winter Park Scenic Boat Tour
unique: A pontoon tour through a chain of lakes and narrow canals, past lakeside mansions and the Rollins College campus, narrated by a local.
buzz: The canals are the charm and the guides are funny. Cheap, shaded and a good break from the heat.

name: Deerfield Island Park
dates: Boat access only; free mainland shuttle Friday–Sunday hourly 10 a.m.–3 p.m.
unique: Broward's only island park is a nature refuge on the Intracoastal Waterway at Hillsboro Boulevard, reachable by private boat or the county's free weekend shuttle rather than by a road entrance.
buzz: The boat crossing and lack of road access are the point. The shuttle operates only Friday through Sunday, and the 3 p.m. departure is the last hourly run, so this needs more timing than an ordinary county-park stop.

name: Florida Panthers at Amerant Bank Arena
dates: Seasonal, generally October–April plus playoffs; published 2026–27 home schedule
company: Florida Panthers and Amerant Bank Arena
customer: Hockey fans, sports travelers, groups, couples
unique: South Florida's NHL team plays its home schedule in Sunrise, with theme nights, rivalry games and the arena's sightlines providing a live ice sport at the edge of the Everglades.
buzz: A rivalry or theme-night game adds to the atmosphere, but dynamically priced seats can move well above the low end of the range. The published 2026–27 calendar confirms an active home season rather than a touring exhibition.

name: Gatorland
unique: A 110-acre alligator park that predates Disney, with a breeding marsh, a boardwalk over thousands of gators and a screaming zipline directly above them.
buzz: It is old Florida and proud of it; the gator wrestling show is a relic and the swamp walk is genuinely good. Cheaper and less crowded than the theme parks.

name: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse and Museum
cost: $15 adult, $12 veteran and senior, $8 ages 6 to 18, free age 5 and under
dates: Tuesday through Sunday 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., last entry 4 p.m., closed Monday
customer: Lighthouse fans, history readers, photographers, families with active children
unique: General admission combines a climb of the working Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse with museum exhibits, outdoor history and an included guided tour, all at the meeting point of the Loxahatchee River and the inlet.
buzz: The climb is the centerpiece, but leave time for the museum and grounds. Guided tours are included on scheduled weekdays, while separate sunrise, sunset and moonrise climbs offer a less ordinary view.

name: Old Davie School Historical Museum
dates: Self-guided Tuesday–Friday 12:30–2:30 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m.–2:30 p.m.; guided tours by appointment
customer: Local-history readers, school groups, architecture visitors
unique: Broward County's oldest existing school building on its original site, built in 1918, holds classrooms, artifacts and exhibits about the settlers, farms and education of early Davie and western Broward.
buzz: The original building makes the local history tangible, but public hours are narrow and morning school programming takes precedence. A guided tour requires booking at least 24 hours ahead.

name: Bulow Plantation Ruins Historic State Park
unique: Coquina walls of a sugar mill and the foundations of a plantation house on Bulow Creek, built in the 1820s by a family that came from the Bahamas, burned in 1836 during the Second Seminole War and left standing in the woods.
buzz: The ruins are more complete than people expect and the story of the war that ended the plantation is the interesting part. It is quiet, shaded and rarely crowded.

name: Camp Blanding Museum and Memorial Park
unique: A museum on a National Guard base that was a World War Two infantry replacement training center, with vehicles, weapons, uniforms, a recreated barracks and a memorial park for the divisions that trained there before shipping out.
buzz: The collection is bigger than people expect for a small Florida town and the volunteers are often veterans. Visitors need to check in at the gate, which surprises some and weeds out the rest.

name: Clearwater Marine Aquarium
unique: A working marine rescue hospital with dolphins, sea turtles and otters, made famous by the Dolphin Tale films.
buzz: The rescue stories are the heart of it and kids connect with the animals. Book tickets online.

name: Coral Castle
unique: A Latvian immigrant single-handedly quarried and moved 1,100 tons of coral rock to build a castle, a rocking chair that weighs tons and a table shaped like Florida, nobody knows how.
buzz: People come for the mystery and leave talking about the loneliness of it; the audio tour tells the story well. Small and strange.

name: Crab Island
unique: A shallow sandbar in the Destin harbor where boats raft up, music plays and people wade in waist deep water, a floating party on the Gulf.
buzz: Rent a pontoon or take a shuttle, bring a cooler and expect a crowd. Not for quiet seekers.

name: Falling Waters State Park
unique: Florida's tallest waterfall, dropping into a hundred foot sinkhole that swallows the creek entirely, with a boardwalk to the overlook, a swimming lake and trails through sandhill and fern covered sinks.
buzz: The waterfall is small by mountain standards and the sinkhole is the story, which the rangers explain. It is a good hour and cheap, and children like the idea of a river disappearing.

name: Flamingo Gardens
unique: A 60 acre botanical garden and wildlife sanctuary with flamingos, a bobcat, otters and a 1930s house, plus a tram through the citrus grove.
buzz: The flamingos and the tram are the kid draw, and the gardens are shady. Good for a hot day.

name: Fort Pierce Inlet State Park
unique: A barrier island park where the Indian River lagoon meets the Atlantic at the inlet, with a swimming beach on the ocean side, a calm lagoon beach for children and a jetty where the fishing and snorkeling are good.
buzz: The lagoon side is the family beach and the ocean side is where the surf is. It is quieter than the public beaches in town and the inlet is the reason the water is clear.

name: Fox Observatory Public Night
dates: Year-round, Saturday after sunset, weather permitting; seasonal closing times
company: South Florida Amateur Astronomers Association at Markham Park
customer: Astronomy beginners, families, photographers, night-sky visitors
unique: Members of a club founded in 1965 open Markham Park's observatory and their telescopes to the public, letting visitors look at planets, the Moon and deep-sky objects with people who know the equipment.
buzz: The volunteer explanations are as useful as the telescope views, and no personal telescope is needed. Cloud cover cancels the value of the trip, and winter sessions end earlier than daylight-saving sessions.

name: Hart Springs
dates: April to September for swimming, campground year round
unique: A county park on the Suwannee with one of the largest spring fed swimming areas in the state, a boardwalk over the run, a campground and a splash pad for children.
buzz: Families come for the shallow swimming area and the campground, and locals say it is the better value than the state parks. The run is clear and the river is beside it.

name: Lake Louisa State Park
unique: Four thousand acres of rolling sandhill, lake and cypress swamp west of Orlando, with a chain of lakes, cabins and a campground, horse trails and paved cycling, in country that looks like the hills of north Florida.
buzz: It is the camping park for Orlando and the hills surprise people who think central Florida is flat. The cabins book out and the lakes are quiet on weekdays.

name: Letchworth-Love Mounds Archaeological State Park
unique: The tallest Native American ceremonial mound in Florida, a fifty one foot platform mound built by people of the Weeden Island culture more than a thousand years ago, with a museum and a trail through the earthworks.
buzz: The mound is bigger than people expect for Florida and the interpretation is careful about what is known and what is not. It is quiet, cheap and usually empty.

name: Orlando Science Center
unique: A hands on science center with a giant dinosaur hall, a planetarium, an observatory and a kids zone, in a modern building near downtown.
buzz: The dinosaur hall and the planetarium are the hits, and it is a good rainy day alternative to the parks.

name: Osceola National Forest
customer: Campers, off road riders, hunters, birders
unique: Two hundred thousand acres of pine flatwoods and cypress swamp between Gainesville and the Georgia line, with a swimming and fishing lake at Ocean Pond, a campground, and miles of sand roads and the Florida Trail running through it.
buzz: It is the closest national forest to Jacksonville and it stays empty. Off road riders use the designated trails, hunters use the season and families camp at Ocean Pond in the shade.

name: Ponce de Leon Springs State Park
unique: A spring run where two springs mix and pour sixty million gallons a day into a swimming basin, with a short trail along Sandy Creek, cypress and tupelo overhead and a picnic area under the oaks.
buzz: It is the cheap swimming hole for Holmes County and the water stays at sixty eight degrees year round. Locals go early on summer weekends because the parking lot fills.

name: Sanford Historic District
unique: A downtown of brick storefronts and a 1920s hotel on the south shore of Lake Monroe, where the St. Johns River becomes navigable, with a riverwalk, a farmers market and a food and drink scene in the old buildings.
buzz: The riverfront and the restored commercial block make it the best downtown in the Orlando area that is not Orlando. People come for brunch and stay for the river.

name: Sawgrass Nature Center and Wildlife Hospital
dates: Year-round; Tuesday–Friday 9 a.m.–5 p.m., weekends 10 a.m.–3 p.m.; closed Monday
company: Sawgrass Nature Center and Wildlife Hospital
unique: A small public nature center supports a working hospital for injured native wildlife, using resident animals and education programs to explain rehabilitation and release rather than presenting a conventional zoo.
buzz: The modest public exhibits and low admission are worth the stop if visitors understand the mission. The wildlife hospital itself is not open for tours because patient stress and safety take priority over spectacle.

name: Sawgrass Recreation Park
unique: An airboat ride into the Everglades with alligators, wading birds and a sawgrass maze, plus a small animal exhibit.
buzz: The airboat is loud and fast and kids love it. The wildlife show is cheesy but the swamp is real.

name: St. Marks Historic Railroad State Trail
unique: Sixteen paved miles on the grade of Florida's first railroad, running from Tallahassee south through the national forest to the old port at St. Marks, where the tracks used to carry cotton to the Gulf.
buzz: It is flat, shaded and free, and the ride into St. Marks ends at a waterfront where the railroad ended. Cyclists do it as a half day and stop for lunch at the coast.

name: Stuart Riverwalk and Downtown
unique: A riverfront town on the St. Lucie with a boardwalk along the water, a downtown of brick storefronts and a reputation as the sailfish capital of the world, with the fleet docks a few blocks away.
buzz: The riverwalk is where the town runs and the restaurants face the water. In sailfish season the docks are full of sportfishing boats and the bars are full of crews.

name: Suwannee River at Old Town
dates: Year round, best spring and fall
company: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and private campgrounds
unique: A stretch of the Suwannee where the river runs wide and black between limestone banks, with public ramps, riverside campgrounds and sturgeon leaping in summer, which is a real hazard and a real spectacle.
buzz: Paddlers do multi day floats and camp on the banks, and anglers fish for bass and catfish. Locals warn about the jumping sturgeon in summer and everybody has a story about one.

name: Tampa Riverwalk
unique: A 2.6 mile paved trail along the Hillsborough River, connecting the aquarium, the history center, parks and the convention center.
buzz: Flat and scenic, with water taxis and good people watching. Best at sunset.

name: Tree Tops Park and Pine Island Ridge
cost: Free; weekend gate fee may apply
dates: Year-round, daily daylight hours; confirm current tower and boardwalk access
unique: Wetland boardwalks, oak hammock, horse trails and an observation tower occupy land once intended for a golf community, with the adjacent Pine Island Ridge natural area adding wooded trails.
buzz: The wetland boardwalk and purple gallinules are reliable reasons for a slow walk, while the tower is a secondary stop. Recent visitor guidance recommends asking staff about current tower and boardwalk access rather than assuming both are open.

name: Cinema Paradiso Hollywood
dates: Year-round; scheduled screenings and festival programs, check current calendar
company: Broward County Film Society and Fort Lauderdale International Film Festival
unique: An 82-seat downtown arthouse screens first-run independent, foreign-language and documentary films, with retrospectives and Fort Lauderdale International Film Festival programming in the same rotation.
buzz: The small room and focused programming are the appeal for viewers who do not want another multiplex screen. Showtimes are film-specific rather than continuous, and Hollywood residents get a Wednesday ticket and popcorn special.

name: Tall Cypress Natural Area
company: Broward County and City of Coral Springs
customer: Walkers, plant and bird visitors, families, photographers
unique: An elevated half-mile boardwalk crosses a preserved basin swamp and pine habitat inside suburban Coral Springs, with interpretive signs and close views into cypress forest without entering the wet ground.
buzz: The short boardwalk is the entire visit and works best as an early or late-hour nature stop. The city lists 68.36 acres, but the public walk samples only a compact portion, which keeps expectations in proportion.

name: Tarpon Springs Sponge Docks
unique: A Greek-American sponge-diving town with working boats, a cathedral, bakeries selling baklava and a museum of the divers who died harvesting the bay.
buzz: The food is the draw, get Greek salad and grilled octopus on the docks; the boat tours are short and touristy.

name: Blue Springs Recreation Area
unique: A county park on the Chipola River where a blue spring boils up into a swimming area, with a sandy beach, a diving platform, tube floats down the river and a campground in the pines.
buzz: Locals swim here all summer and the tube float is the ritual. It is cheap, the water is cold and the spring is the reason people drive from Dothan.

name: Clewiston and Lake Okeechobee
cost: Free, marina and guide fees extra
dates: Year round, best winter and spring
company: City of Clewiston and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
unique: America's sweetest town, built on sugar cane, on the south shore of Lake Okeechobee, with a marina, a fishing pier and a rim canal where the bass fishing is famous and the cane fields run to the horizon.
buzz: Bass anglers come from other states and the guides are booked in winter. The sugar mill and the cane smoke are part of the landscape and the town is honest about both.

name: Crystal River Archaeological State Park
unique: A 14 acre mound complex built by the Woodland culture 1,500 years ago, with burial mounds, a plaza and a museum on the river.
buzz: The mounds are subtle but the story is fascinating, and the river setting is pretty. Combine it with a manatee swim.

name: De Soto National Memorial
unique: The presumed landing site of Hernando de Soto's 1539 expedition, with a visitor center on the conquest of La Florida, a living history camp in season where rangers wear armor, and a trail along the Manatee River.
buzz: The rangers in period armor are the part children remember and the exhibits do not romanticize the expedition. It is free, on the water and rarely crowded.

name: Dunns Creek State Park
unique: Six thousand acres where Dunns Creek runs into Crescent Lake, with a spring run, cypress swamp, sandhill and a paddle trail through water that is black with tannin and full of birds.
buzz: Paddlers and birders use it and it stays quiet because there is almost no development. The creek is narrow and the swamp is close on both sides.

name: Flagler Beach Pier
unique: A wooden pier over an orange coquina sand beach, with a restaurant at the foot of it, surfers on the north side and anglers working the pilings for whiting and flounder.
buzz: The coquina sand is the local curiosity, orange and coarse, and the pier is where the town gathers. It is one of the few Florida beach towns with a low rise skyline still.

name: Havana Antique and Vintage Trail
company: Visit Gadsden County and the Havana merchants
unique: A self guided trail through a town that burned in 1916 and rebuilt in brick, now a row of antique shops, design stores and cafes along the main street, in a county that was also the state's shade tobacco capital.
buzz: Dealers say the furniture prices are better than Tallahassee and the town has kept its scale. People come for one shop and spend the afternoon.

name: Jacksonville Beach
unique: A wide Atlantic beach with a pier, surf shops, a boardwalk and a cluster of bars and restaurants, twenty minutes from downtown.
buzz: The pier is the landmark and the surf is consistent. Parking is easier than most Florida beaches.

name: Monticello Historic District
unique: A courthouse town of brick storefronts and antebellum and Victorian houses on a grid of live oak streets, in the county seat of one of the oldest cotton counties in Florida, twenty five miles east of Tallahassee.
buzz: The houses are the attraction and the town is quiet enough to walk alone. People who live in Tallahassee drive over for the square and the bed and breakfast.

name: Mount Dora
unique: A hilltop lake town with antique shops, a boardwalk, a historic inn and a steam train, in a part of Florida that has hills.
buzz: The downtown is walkable and the lakefront is pretty, with festivals most weekends in season.

name: Navarre Beach Sea Turtle Conservation Center
company: Navarre Beach Sea Turtle Conservation Center
unique: A small center on the barrier island with resident sea turtles that cannot be released, a working rehabilitation space and staff who explain why a plastic bag looks like a jellyfish and what to do with a stranded turtle.
buzz: Children remember the turtles by name and parents like that the message is conservation rather than a photo op. It is small, cheap and close to the beach.

name: Olustee Battlefield Historic State Park
customer: Civil War travellers, families, school groups
unique: The ground of Florida's largest Civil War battle, fought in February 1864 when Confederate forces stopped a Union advance toward Tallahassee, with earthworks, a museum and a monument inside the pine flatwoods.
buzz: The February reenactment draws thousands and the rest of the year the field is empty. The museum explains why a battle this far south mattered, which most accounts skip.

name: Peace River at Arcadia
dates: Year round, best November to May
unique: A blackwater river with a public ramp at Arcadia where paddlers dig for fossil shark teeth in the gravel bars, float past cypress and cattle pasture and finish at a riverside bar.
buzz: The fossil hunting is the local obsession and the gravel bars give up teeth after every flood. It is slow water, easy for beginners, and the outfitters run shuttles.

name: Wild Florida Airboats and Gator Park
unique: An airboat run out of a working cattle ranch on the headwaters of the Everglades, with a drive through safari of exotic hoofstock, a gator park and an airboat ride through marsh and cypress where alligators and bald eagles are the standard sightings.
buzz: The airboat is the reason and the gator show is the part children remember. It is a commercial operation and honest about it, and the headwaters marsh is genuinely wild once the boat gets going.

name: Amelia Island Museum of History
unique: A county museum in the old Nassau County jail, telling eight flags of Amelia Island history, the Timucua, the shrimp industry and the shrimping families, with a cell block left in place.
buzz: The jail building is half the fun and the eight flags story is genuinely complicated. Volunteers tell it well and children like the cells.

name: Cassadaga Spiritualist Camp
unique: A Victorian camp of mediums and healers in the pine scrub, with a bookstore, a hotel and readings you can book like a haircut.
buzz: Skeptics and believers both enjoy the earnest weirdness; readings vary wildly in quality. Walk the lake at dusk.

name: Cocoa Beach Pier
unique: A 800 foot pier over the Atlantic with restaurants, a surf shop and a view back at the space center launches.
buzz: Good for a walk and a drink, and the surf below is beginner friendly. Parking costs.

name: Forest Capital Museum State Park
unique: A museum on the county that calls itself the forest capital of the south, with a walk through longleaf pine forest, a sawmill display, turpentine stills and a Cracker homestead with a dogtrot cabin and a sugar cane mill.
buzz: The Cracker homestead outdoors is the part children like and the forestry exhibits explain a whole economy. It is cheap, quiet and specific to a place most people drive past.

name: Green Cove Springs Riverfront
unique: A city park on the St. Johns built around a sulfur spring that once drew steamboat crowds to a resort hotel, with a spring fed swimming pool on the river, a long pier and a shady waterfront.
buzz: The pool on the river is the reason people come and the steamboat history is the reason the town looks the way it does. It is cheap and the river is wide and brown and slow.

name: Kissimmee Lakefront Park and Downtown
unique: A lakefront park on Lake Tohopekaliga with a fishing pier, a playground, a splash pad and a promenade into a downtown of brick storefronts, a few minutes from the theme parks and nothing like them.
buzz: It is where local families go instead of the parks. The lake is big, the sunsets are good and the parking is free, which in Kissimmee is the whole pitch.

name: LaBelle and the Caloosahatchee
dates: Year round; Swamp Cabbage Festival in February
unique: A river town on the Caloosahatchee with a waterfront park, a public dock where boats run to the Gulf, and a February festival built around swamp cabbage, the heart of the sabal palm, cooked with ham hock.
buzz: The festival is the county's signature and the river is the everyday. Boaters use LaBelle as a stop between the lake and Fort Myers and the town is used to them.

name: Lake Okeechobee at Moore Haven
cost: Free, ramp and guide fees extra
dates: Year round, best winter and spring
company: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and Glades County
unique: A stretch of the second largest freshwater lake wholly in the United States, seen from the top of the Herbert Hoover Dike, with a public ramp, a fishing pier and waterfowl moving through the shallows in winter.
