buzz: The lake is so big it reads as a sea and the dike gives the only view. Anglers fish the rim canal and birders work the marsh on the west side.

name: Man in the Sea Museum
unique: A small museum of diving history on the site of the Navy's first experimental diving unit, with a submarine, a diving bell, helmets and suits and the story of how saturation diving and the SEALAB programs were worked out here.
buzz: Divers and Navy people come for the equipment and children like the submarine they can climb into. It is small, cheap and run by volunteers who know the history firsthand.

name: Mounts Botanical Garden
cost: $20 adult, $18 senior, college student and military, $13 ages 6 to 17, free under 6
dates: Tuesday through Sunday 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., last entry 3 p.m., closed Monday and some holidays
company: Friends of Mounts Botanical Garden and Palm Beach County
customer: Gardeners, photographers, plant people, families, tropical plant beginners
unique: Palm Beach County's botanical garden concentrates tropical and subtropical plants into a walkable collection of themed gardens, with seasonal evening hours extending visits on selected summer nights.
buzz: Go near opening for cooler walking conditions. The last regular entry is an hour before closing, and summer Golden Hours run until 8 p.m. on Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays through August.

name: Peace River Wildlife Center
unique: A rehabilitation center for injured birds and small wildlife, with pelicans, owls, eagles and a turtle pond, run by volunteers.
buzz: Small and free, with staff who explain each animal's story. Good for kids.

name: Quincy Historic District
unique: A courthouse square and surrounding streets with one of the largest collections of antebellum and Victorian houses in north Florida, built on the shade tobacco economy that made Gadsden County rich.
buzz: The houses are the attraction and the tobacco history is what explains them. The downtown is quiet and the walking tour takes about an hour.

name: Werner-Boyce Salt Springs
unique: A coastal spring and salt marsh park with a deep spring, paddling trails and a boardwalk, hidden behind the commercial strip.
buzz: The spring is a surprise and the paddle is quiet. Bring bug spray.

name: Plantation Historical Museum
dates: Year-round, Wednesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; closed Sunday–Tuesday
company: City of Plantation and Plantation Historical Society
unique: A volunteer-supported city museum on Fig Tree Lane concentrates on Plantation's development and community collections, offering a small-scale record of a suburb whose history is usually overlooked between Fort Lauderdale and Davie.
buzz: This is a short local stop rather than a regional destination museum. Visitors value the volunteer explanations and free admission, and pairing it with another Broward historical site makes a more substantial afternoon.

name: Arcadia Historic Downtown
unique: A downtown of 1900s brick storefronts and a courthouse on a live oak shaded square, in a cattle and citrus town that calls itself the city of oaks and hosts one of the oldest rodeos in the state.
buzz: The antique shops are the draw and the oaks are the setting. Rodeo weekend fills the town and the rest of the year it is quiet.

name: Blackwater Heritage State Trail
unique: A paved nine mile rail trail from Milton through the old lumber town of Bagdad to the naval air station, on the grade of the Florida and Alabama Railroad, with pine woods and the Blackwater River on either side.
buzz: It is flat, shaded in stretches and free, which makes it the default ride for people in Milton. The Bagdad end has the old mill town houses.

name: Cape San Blas Lighthouse
unique: A lighthouse and two keeper's quarters moved off the eroding Cape and rebuilt in town, where you can climb the tower for a view over St. Joseph Bay and read about the hurricanes that forced the move.
buzz: The story of moving the light is as interesting as the climb. Photographers shoot it at sunset and the bay behind it is shallow and glassy.

name: Central Florida Zoo and Botanical Gardens
company: Central Florida Zoo and Botanical Gardens
unique: A zoo that started as a roadside collection in 1923 on the shores of Lake Monroe, with a Florida black bear exhibit, a sloth and a botanical garden of native plants, small enough to walk in an afternoon.
buzz: Parents like that it is walkable and not exhausting, and the splash pad saves summer afternoons. It is a local zoo rather than a destination one, priced accordingly.

name: Falling Creek Falls
unique: A fifteen foot waterfall dropping into a rocky basin at the end of a boardwalk through cypress and ferns, one of the few true waterfalls in the Florida flatwoods.
buzz: It is a five minute walk and free, and the boardwalk makes it easy. People find it on the way to the springs and are surprised by the rock.

name: Gadsden Arts Center
unique: A regional art museum and galleries in a restored building on Quincy's square, with changing exhibitions of Florida and southeastern artists and a permanent collection of work by artists with Gadsden County roots.
buzz: The exhibitions change often and the space is better than a town this size usually has. Locals treat it as the cultural anchor of the county.

name: Horseshoe Beach
unique: A fishing village on a hook of land at the edge of the Big Bend, with a boat ramp, a few docks, no high rises and a west facing beach where the sun sets over the marsh instead of the ocean.
buzz: Anglers launch here for the flats and the offshore rocks, and families come for the shallow water and the quiet. It is the kind of Florida town that has not been rebuilt for tourists.

name: Iguanaland and Iguana Fest
unique: A reptile park devoted to iguanas and their relatives, with an annual Iguana Fest of animal encounters and vendors, a niche so specific it becomes a destination.
buzz: Small and earnest; keepers are generous with handling opportunities. The festival is a local street-party vibe rather than a convention.

name: Military Museum of North Florida
unique: A collection of vehicles, aircraft parts, uniforms and personal items from every American war, housed in the old barracks buildings of a decommissioned naval station on the St. Johns.
buzz: Volunteers run it and will talk you through the collection. The setting in the old base buildings is half the experience.

name: Okeechobee Lakefront and Fishing Pier
dates: Year round, best winter and spring
unique: A city park and pier on the north shore of the lake, with a long fishing pier out into the rim canal, a campground, and a view across water that goes to the horizon in every direction.
buzz: Anglers fish the pier for crappie and bluegill and the lake itself for bass. It is cheap, flat and the sunsets over the water are the local ritual.

name: Palatka Riverfront
unique: A downtown on a bend of the St. Johns with a river walk, a city dock, a 1900s courthouse and blocks of brick commercial buildings from the steamboat years when Palatka was the gateway to the interior.
buzz: The river is the reason to walk it and the town has kept its bones. Anglers fish the dock and the boats go by all day.

name: Pine Log State Forest
unique: Florida's first state forest, bought during the Depression, with longleaf pine, a chain of small lakes, a campground and trails for bikes and horses in the sandhills north of Chipley.
buzz: It is quiet, cheap and used mostly by locals with horses and mountain bikes. The lakes fish well and the campground is small enough to feel private.

name: The Villages
cost: Free to visit, golf and food extra
dates: Year round; town squares open to the public
customer: The merely curious, visiting families, retirees
unique: The largest retirement community in the country, a hundred thousand people across three counties with its own town squares, golf cart paths, nightly live music and a scale of planned living that has to be seen to be believed.
buzz: It is either a utopia or a cautionary tale depending on who you ask, and both are worth a look. Visitors describe the golf cart traffic and the free nightly bands on the squares as the most Florida thing they have ever seen.

name: Apalachicola River at Blountstown
dates: Year round, best spring and fall
company: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
unique: A wide, slow stretch of the Apalachicola below the Blountstown bluff, with a public ramp, cypress and tupelo along the banks and a bass and catfish fishery that locals keep to themselves.
buzz: Anglers fish the dead water around the bars and paddlers work upstream against a current that is barely there. There are no facilities, so it stays local.

name: Constitution Convention Museum State Park
unique: A small museum where Florida's first constitution was drafted in 1838, with a walk through exhibit, period rooms and a ranger who will explain why a territory of forty thousand people needed a constitution before it could become a state.
buzz: It is tiny and the ranger makes it. People visiting the coast for the beach are surprised to find the state's founding document was written here.

name: Paynes Creek Historic State Park
unique: The site of a trading post and fort built in 1849 after the last outbreak of the Second Seminole War, where two storekeepers were killed, with a museum, earthworks and a trail along Paynes Creek.
buzz: It is small, free and almost unknown, and the story of a fort built for a war that was already ending is the interesting part. The creek is good for a short walk.

name: Sebring Downtown Circle
unique: A 1920s planned downtown built around a circular park with a bandshell at the center and a ring of Mediterranean revival storefronts, laid out when the town was a winter resort for northerners.
buzz: The circle is the photograph and the bandshell still hosts concerts. Race weekends fill it with visitors who otherwise would never see the town.

name: Monument of States
unique: A twenty five foot concrete tower built in 1943 from stones sent by every state and several countries, with a plaque for each, standing in a small park as a wartime monument to the union of the states.
buzz: People stop because it looks odd from the road and stay to find their own state's stone. It takes ten minutes and the story of how it was built is the reward.

name: Spook Hill
unique: A gravity hill where you put your car in neutral and appear to roll uphill, with a painted sign and a local legend about an alligator and a pirate.
buzz: It is silly and free and works exactly as promised; kids love it. A five minute stop on the way to Bok Tower.

name: Lake City Downtown
unique: A downtown of brick commercial buildings, a 1900s courthouse and a historic hotel block, in a town that was a railroad and tobacco center and now feeds off the interstate and the springs.
buzz: The historic district is small and the restaurants are local. People stop on the way to Ichetucknee and find the town better than the exit ramp suggests.

name: Marianna Courthouse Square
unique: A square with an 1900s courthouse in the middle and a ring of storefronts, in a town that was a crossroads for both armies and later a peanut and timber market, with antebellum houses on the streets behind it.
buzz: The square is small and the houses around it are the real architecture. People stop on the way to the caverns and find more than they expected.

name: New River at Lake Butler
company: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
unique: A blackwater river with a public access near Lake Butler, running through swamp and timberland where the current is slow and the cypress is thick.
buzz: Local paddlers and anglers use it and almost nobody else does. The ramp is basic and the water is dark and quiet.

name: Perry Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse and a ring of storefronts in a town that has been logging and milling the Big Bend for a century and a half, with the forest products industry still running the county.
buzz: It is a working timber town rather than a tourist one, and the square shows it. People stop for supplies on the way to the coast.

name: Bonifay Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse, a monument and a few storefronts in the seat of a peanut and cattle county at the top of the state, where the springs are the only reason most people get off the interstate.
buzz: Small, hot and quiet. It is a place to buy a cold drink on the way to Vortex or Ponce de Leon.

name: Chipley Downtown
unique: A small grid of brick storefronts and a courthouse, in a town that grew on the railroad and the turpentine and lumber trade and now sits at the crossroads of two highways with the state's tallest waterfall a few miles south.
buzz: Two blocks and a couple of cafes. Most people pass through on the way to the park.

name: Live Oak Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse, a ring of storefronts and a monument, in a town that has been the seat of a timber and farming county since the railroad came through in the 1860s.
buzz: Small and working, with the festival traffic keeping the restaurants busy. People walk it between shows.

name: Blountstown Courthouse Square
unique: A small square with a 1930s courthouse and a few storefronts a few blocks from the Apalachicola River, in the seat of one of the poorest and least visited counties in Florida.
buzz: Two blocks, one cafe and a river ramp at the end of the street. People pass through on the way to the national forest and the springs.

name: Bristol Courthouse Square
unique: A small square with a 1900s courthouse and a handful of stores in the seat of one of Florida's least populated counties, ten minutes from the bluffs and the river.
buzz: Two blocks and a gas station, and the people are used to hikers buying water. It is the last stop before Torreya.

name: Cross City Courthouse Square
unique: A small square with a 1930s courthouse, a monument and a few stores at the crossroads of the county, in a place built by timber, turpentine and the railroad.
buzz: Two blocks and a diner. It is a stop for ice on the way to Horseshoe Beach or the river.

name: Jasper Courthouse Square
unique: A square with an 1900s courthouse, a monument and a few storefronts, in a town that sits where the Georgia line meets the Suwannee country and has been a crossroads since the railroad came through.
buzz: Two blocks and a couple of places to eat. It is a stop between the state parks and the interstate.

name: Macclenny Downtown
unique: A small grid of brick storefronts and a 1900s courthouse in the seat of a county that is mostly national forest, timber and the interstate, with a railroad running through the middle of town.
buzz: Two blocks and a couple of places to eat. It is a stop between the forest and the highway.

name: Mayo Courthouse Square
unique: A small square with a 1900s courthouse, a monument and a handful of stores, in one of the smallest county seats in Florida, a few miles from the Suwannee and the blue spring.
buzz: Two blocks and a grocery store, and the people are used to people in wet swimsuits. It is the last stop before the river.

name: Wauchula Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1920s courthouse and a ring of storefronts in a county built on cattle, citrus and the Peace River, in a town whose name comes from a Creek word for wild turkey.
buzz: Two blocks and a diner, and the people are used to nobody stopping. The square is shaded and the courthouse lawn is where the town gathers.

name: Lake Butler Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1930s courthouse, a monument and a few stores in a county that has more state prison beds than residents and still runs on timber and cattle.
buzz: Two blocks and one restaurant. It is a place to stop between Gainesville and the Okefenokee road.

name: Starke Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse, a monument and a ring of storefronts in a town that calls itself the peach capital and sits at the crossroads of two highways north of Gainesville.
buzz: Small and plain, with a restaurant or two that serve the courthouse crowd. People stop on the way to the springs.

name: Trenton Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse and a few storefronts, in a county with more springs than towns and a courthouse that sits between the peanut fields and the Suwannee.
buzz: Two blocks, a diner and a hardware store. People stop for supplies before the springs.
